summary: Travelling up through Italy with Harold Mellor in April 1900, Wilde stopped three days at Naples and wrote to Robert Ross that he had fallen in love with a Sea-God, joking that the young man was for some extraordinary reason at the Regia Marina School instead of being with Triton. In the same breath he notes that most of his Naples friends are in prison. Nothing further about the young man appears in the pages read: no name, no age, no outcome.

sources.quote: At Naples we stopped three days. Most of my friends are, as you know, in prison, but I met some of nice memory, and fell in love with a Sea-God, who for some extraordinary reason is at the Regia Marina School, instead of being with Triton.
sources.context: Wilde to Robert Ross, 16 April [1900], from Rome - a travel narrative running from Palermo through Naples to the Easter pilgrimage at the Vatican. 'H. M.' in the next paragraph is Harold Mellor, his travelling companion.
sources.supports: The whole of the record: Wilde's own statement that he fell in love, the young man's institution, and the absence of any recorded outcome
sources.citation_provenance: PDF p. 1225. The letter's heading (recipient, date, address) stands on an earlier printed page; the page read carries the editors' footnote 'Easter Day 1900 was on 15 April'.

manuscript.repository: William Andrews Clark Memorial Library, UCLA
